mcqs.question: What happens to a current‑carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field?

options.A: It experiences a force perpendicular to both the field and the current direction
options.B: It only heats up due to resistance

mcqs.answer: It experiences a force perpendicular to both the field and the current direction
mcqs.explanation: The magnetic force on a current‑carrying conductor is given by F = I L × B. The direction of the force is perpendicular to both the direction of current (L) and the magnetic field (B), as described by Fleming’s left‑hand rule. Hence option A is correct; the other options describe unrelated effects.

mcqs.question: According to Fleming’s left‑hand rule, if the magnetic field is directed from north to south and the current in the conductor flows upward, in which direction does the force act on the conductor?
mcqs.explanation: First finger (field) points toward the south, second finger (current) points upward. With the left hand positioned this way, the thumb points toward the west, indicating the direction of the force. Therefore option B is correct; the other directions do not follow the rule.

mcqs.question: Which statement best distinguishes the principle of an electric motor from that of a simple electromagnet?

options.A: An electric motor converts electrical energy into mechanical rotation using the force on a current‑carrying conductor in a magnetic field, whereas an electromagnet only produces a magnetic field when current flows
options.B: Both devices store electrical energy for later use
options.C: An electromagnet rotates while a motor remains stationary
options.D: Both rely on chemical reactions to generate motion

mcqs.answer: An electric motor converts electrical energy into mechanical rotation using the force on a current‑carrying conductor in a magnetic field, whereas an electromagnet only produces a magnetic field when current flows
mcqs.explanation: A motor’s essential principle is the conversion of electrical energy to mechanical motion via the magnetic force on a conductor (Fleming’s left‑hand rule). An electromagnet merely creates a magnetic field when current passes through it and does not produce continuous motion. Hence option A correctly captures the distinction; the other options are inaccurate.

mcqs.question: Which of the following lists the main components of a simple DC electric motor in the correct order from the power source to the moving part?

options.A: Battery → Commutator → Armature → Brushes → Magnetic field
options.B: Battery → Brushes → Commutator → Armature → Magnetic field
options.C: Battery → Armature → Commutator → Brushes → Magnetic field
options.D: Battery → Magnetic field → Armature → Commutator → Brushes

mcqs.answer: Battery → Brushes → Commutator → Armature → Magnetic field
mcqs.explanation: In a DC motor, the battery supplies current to the brushes, which make contact with the commutator. The commutator transfers the current to the armature (the rotating coil) that sits within the magnetic field. Option B follows this sequence; the other options place components in an incorrect order.

mcqs.question: In a simple motor a rectangular coil is placed in a uniform magnetic field and connected to a battery. Which description correctly explains how continuous rotation is achieved?

options.A: The coil experiences a torque in one direction, and the commutator reverses the current each half‑turn, keeping the torque in the same rotational sense
options.B: The coil experiences a torque that stops after half a turn because the magnetic forces cancel, so the motor ceases
options.C: The coil does not experience any torque because the magnetic field is uniform
options.D: The coil’s torque direction alternates, causing it to oscillate back and forth without completing a full rotation

mcqs.answer: The coil experiences a torque in one direction, and the commutator reverses the current each half‑turn, keeping the torque in the same rotational sense
mcqs.explanation: When current flows, the coil experiences a torque. After half a rotation the split‑ring commutator reverses the direction of current, so the torque continues to act in the same rotational direction, producing continuous rotation. Options B, C and D describe outcomes that do not occur in a functioning motor.

mcqs.question: A straight vertical wire carries a current of 5 A. It is placed in a uniform magnetic field of 0.2 T directed into the page. What is the direction of the magnetic force on the wire?
mcqs.explanation: Using Fleming’s left‑hand rule: first finger (field) points into the page, second finger (current) points upward. The thumb then points toward the left, indicating the direction of the force. Hence option B is correct; the other directions do not follow the rule.

mcqs.question: A student says that reversing the direction of current in a conductor while keeping the external magnetic field unchanged also reverses the magnetic field produced around the conductor. Which statement correctly addresses this misconception using Fleming’s left‑hand rule?

options.A: Reversing the current reverses the direction of the magnetic field produced by the conductor, but the force direction remains the same
options.B: Reversing the current reverses both the magnetic field around the conductor and the direction of the force on the conductor
options.C: Reversing the current does not affect the magnetic field around the conductor; only the external magnetic field matters for the force
options.D: Reversing the current reverses the direction of the magnetic field around the conductor, and consequently the force direction also reverses

mcqs.answer: Reversing the current reverses the direction of the magnetic field around the conductor, and consequently the force direction also reverses
mcqs.explanation: The magnetic field produced by a current‑carrying wire follows the right‑hand rule; reversing current flips that field. In Fleming’s left‑hand rule, the force direction depends on both the external field and the current direction, so reversing current also reverses the force. Option D captures both effects; the other options are partially or wholly incorrect.

mcqs.question: Why does a split‑ring commutator enable a simple DC motor to keep rotating in the same direction instead of oscillating back and forth?

options.A: It periodically reverses the direction of the external magnetic field
options.B: It switches the direction of current in the armature coil each half turn, ensuring the torque always acts in the same rotational sense
options.C: It changes the polarity of the battery each half turn
options.D: It reduces the magnetic field strength during each half turn

mcqs.answer: It switches the direction of current in the armature coil each half turn, ensuring the torque always acts in the same rotational sense
mcqs.explanation: The split‑ring commutator reverses the current in the armature after each half‑turn. This reversal makes the magnetic force (torque) continue to act in the same rotational direction, producing continuous rotation. Options A, C and D describe mechanisms that are not part of a DC motor’s operation.
